name: std::iota

declarations.code:
template <class ForwardIt, class T>

void iota(ForwardIt first, ForwardIt last, T value);

sections.title: Parameters
sections.text:
first, last

 -

 the range of elements to fill with sequentially increasing values starting with value


 value

 -

 initial value to store

sections.title: Complexity
sections.text: Exactly std::distance(first, last) increments and assignments.

sections.title: Possible implementation
Notes
sections.text: The function is named after the integer function ⍳  from the programming language APL. It was one of the STL components that were not included in C++98, but made it into the standard library in C++11.

summary: Fills the range [first, last) with sequentially increasing values, starting with value and repetitively evaluating ++value.

guides.name: std::iota
guides.summary: Fill a sequence with consecutive values.
guides.analogy: Like numbering a row of seats, starting with a number you choose.
guides.signature:
template<class ForwardIt, class T>
void iota(ForwardIt first, ForwardIt last, T value);
guides.note: The destination must already have space. iota assigns values; it does not grow the collection.
